source_span: Agents compress the switching cost that used to be booked as a consumer moat. This phenomenon is exactly why we like being short Consumer Inertia (GSXUSWCH).
source_chain: Muse adoption is surging (1.6M US downloads in 8 days, ~2x ChatGPT's first-8-days pace) therefore agents compress the switching cost that used to be booked as a consumer moat therefore Miller likes being short Consumer Inertia (GSXUSWCH), which is approaching its lows as agentic-AI narrative momentum builds. No explicit invalidation is stated for the short itself.
pulse_chain: Muse hit #1 on the US free iPhone chart within a week of its Sept 8 release therefore agents move activity off human-facing screens onto the compute plumbing, exposing any business earning a return from friction/complexity/inertia therefore Goldman's Miller is short the Consumer Inertia basket on that logic (basket -2.58% Tuesday, led lower by PLNT/NYT/SCHW/ALL/INTU) therefore the read is contested and unresolved: it settles on whether inertia names keep falling once compute names stop rising, with JPMorgan (O'Dwyer) disputing the bank-sector read specifically and turning outright bearish on the broader theme only on a consumer break or an AI capex cut.
why: The pulse reproduces Miller's chain (Muse adoption -> agents compress switching costs -> short Consumer Inertia) with correct attribution, tickers and figures matching the source and the Jeter desk-color note, and layers in JPMorgan's O'Dwyer dispute (no threat to bank unit economics, positioning unwind not re-rating, fade toward MS/PNC/FITB) without reversing any step, misattributing a bank, or inventing a mechanism neither note argues.
